articles.title: TikTok Roundup: Foot Fungus, Butt Injections, and The Wedding Dress From Hell
articles.description: This week's viral drama: the Undone by Kate wedding dress controversy. A bride named Alexander Mae made a series of TikToks about her "wedding dress from hell." To sum it up, the dress designer that she hired was an unprofessional mess who was late and made a crappy dress. Although Mae didn't name the brand, designer Kate March, owner of the brand Undone by Kate, come forward to reveal herself. March made her own video , in which she claimed that she gave the bride a full refund. However, the date that she issued the refund wasn't until after Mae made the wedding-dress-from-hell posts. Kate also hasn't beat the allegations of being kind of a shitty seamstress. Alix Earle allegedly got some sort of a BBL or fat injections in her butt. She has denied it, which fans think is a little odd because she has admitted to getting boob implants. https://instagram.com/p/Dav-oaEGcz7 Sablé Boulangerie is a trendy boutique pastry shop in Arizona that has a popular social media presence. Unfortunately, its creator and chef, Will Porter, is also a member of the manosphere who supports renowned misogynist Andrew Tate. Porter appeared in a Jubilee debate video in which he showed support for Tate and for the looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular. https://instagram.com/p/DbECfsjAnQg Here we go, ONTD will love this one. A woman on a cruise was filmed in the ship restaurant scratching her foot fungus with her bare hands, then using a metal fork or spoon to scratch it. A video went viral of a woman's Belgian Malinois chasing a man and his pit bull as they frantically try to escape. The owner of the Malinois makes practically zero effort to hold back her damn dog. And, oop, just a few days later, footage surfaced of another incident that appears to involve the same dog and the same woman in the same apartment complex. Do you remember Nick Baumel, the medical student who made TikToks that used misogynist language for female genitalia and joked about judging a certain medical condition common in gay men? He made a new TikTok in which he says that he attempted suicide because of the online bullying. He criticized doctors who "know nothing about him," for "lecturing me and my generation on compassion and empathy while they're publicly shaming an LGBTQ medical student into ending his life." Except...those doctors did not shame Baumel for being gay, nor did they call for him to harm himself. They criticized his misogyny and lack of professionalism. Baumel claims that he made the offensive TikToks for women and LGBTQ men, who are "my people." Baumel has still never apologized. He is now a practicing doctor, by the way. This girl named Alana went viral for eating a watermelon in a weird way while cosplaying as the baby from Ice Age . https://instagram.com/p/DaxhOGuS3si Nic and Olandria from Love Island have broken up . They made it to about the one-year mark of the time they got together, prompting speculation that they were -- hold back your tears -- only together to make more money as influencers. BookTok Roundup: -Author, activist, and actress Amanda Seales revealed that Issa Rae did not invite her on the Insecure reunion tour. What she did not get into is that she has publicly talked shit about Issa Rae. So, the response was like, what did you expect? -The novel Haunting Adeline , by H.D. Carlton, is being adapted into a movie, to much controversy , debate and excitement . It is about a woman who falls in love with the stalker who sexually assaults her. -Tomi Adeyemi, author of the novel Children of Blood and Bone , has denounced the upcoming film adaptation, which stars Amandla Stenberg. Previously, Adeyemi defended Stenberg's casting, even though Amandla is a light-skinned biracial actress and the character she plays is described as dark-skinned in the book. -AI porn ads, often featuring dark fantasy themes, have become common on TikTok. Some of them depict outright rape and violence against women. One actually showed a woman having sex with a demon snake creature. Many users have noticed these ads and have even tried reporting them to TikTok, apparently to no avail. -Some wank going back and forth on BookTok for the past few weeks is whether using big words is ableist . Do you enjoy your local indie coffee shop? Maybe a quaint mom-and-pop joint, or an eclectic artsy dive -- heck, maybe even a bougie hipster place with white subway tile? Because lately TikTok has been on a kick of shit-talking their local indie coffeehouses. Several commentators have complained that the coffee at their local places is always bad, too watered down, or too expensive. Not sure if this is just kind of a spontaneous trend, if Big Coffee somehow has a hand in this, or if a lot of indie coffee shops just kind of suck right now. Sucks for them, because I have some great ones by me, and I do love a bougie iced latte. 💅 A few big influencers got married: The first is fashion influencer Paige Lorenze and tennis player Tommy Paul. https://instagram.com/p/DbDC70yknu6 The next is Danielle Walter, a dating content creator who fell in love with a Brazilian Uber driver and spiritual guru, got engaged after less than a year, and got married four months after getting engaged. https://instagram.com/p/DbL8wuGjx83 And I didn't cover it, but influencer Micarah Tewers also got married last month: https://instagram.com/p/DaLEvYPRoH3 Saucy Santana, the creator of the "quiet on the creek" meme, already dropped a song version, which climbed to #1 on the TikTok viral songs chart. TikTokers were debating what the phrase meant, whether it had some secret meaning, and whether it was an AAVE phrase that white people had appropriated. It, in fact, does just mean "quiet on the creek."
